title: Holding MutexGuard across await points
prompt: Why does holding a standard MutexGuard across an await point make the surrounding future non-Send?
answer: `std::sync::MutexGuard` does not implement Send because some operating systems require a mutex to be unlocked on the same thread that locked it. A multi-threaded async runtime can resume a future on a different thread after an await point. If a MutexGuard is alive across that yield, the future cannot be moved across threads and fails the Send bound.
